checks.quote: # Distinguishing Target Inhibition, Substrate Competition, and Reporter Interference in a Coupled Fluorescence Assay
checks.reason: No proposal to consult prior target/reporter Methods, supplements or a validated protocol before execution and check transfer of detailed conditions.

Two independent incorrect propositions: fluorescence loss in an enzyme-free spike is not specific proof of an inner-filter effect (quenching/chemical change also lower it); a linear Stern-Volmer intensity plot does not distinguish dynamic from static quenching. Primary experimental support: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6959846/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5761004/.
Available purified enzymes and UV stock quantification do not verify enzyme/compound identities, purity or active preparation integrity before inference.

No original buffer, cofactors, temperature or reaction volume is supplied and no concrete selection/calibration procedure resolves them; detailed later concentration ratios do not supply this prerequisite.
No primary product amount/concentration and time unit convention or complete weak/missing quantitative endpoint rule.
Technical versus day replication is distinguished, but fixed counts have no variance/precision/power justification.
Randomization is present; no concealed coding/blinded analysis or equivalent locked bias-control procedure.
Lists global models and parameter CIs but does not specify independent-day/nested-well treatment or free-inhibitor assumptions before interpreting ordinary inhibition fits.
Concentration ranges and acceptance criteria are given, but no lock of the pilot-selected ranges/windows/model rules before independent confirmatory testing.
Failure repairs are given without refreezing the revised procedure and testing new independent confirmation data.

No-change orthogonal rate is taken as proof of no target inhibition without adequate-precision equivalence; reduced product also needs substrate/product side chemistry exclusion. Threefold IC50 agreement alone is not an identifying decision.

Names a direct orthogonal assay but does not operationally validate analyte recovery, matrix suppression/interference and target-incubation product stability. Merely avoiding fluorescence does not establish independent accuracy.
Plate map and calibration measurements are useful but not a linked raw-file/sample-ID and versioned code/settings audit trail.
Prospective active vehicle, omissions, product/fluorophore spike, reporter bypass and conditional known-inhibitor controls explain their distinct roles.
